$comment: to the route that serves it, or records why it has none.
This file exists so that a screen in the inventory cannot go unruled-on. It
does NOT claim a screen is well built - only that somebody decided what
happens to it. check-screen-inventory.mjs fails when the inventory grows an
ID this file does not mention, when this file names a route the router does
not have, or when it mentions an ID the inventory no longer contains.
'route' means the router serves it at that path.
'within' means it is a step or section of that route, not a screen of its
own - the wizard's steps are the clearest case.
'absent' means the portal does not have it, with the reason. An absent entry
is a recorded gap, not an excuse: FRONTEND-TASKS.md is where they get fixed.
Admin-only prefixes (ADM APR INS PVO REP ROL SYS USR) are out of this lane
entirely - see ebpco-citizen-web-frontend-only. The gate ignores them.

PUB-001.absent: Splash is a mobile app concept - a web page loads directly. Mobile owns PUB-001.

PUB-007.absent: DELIBERATE, and load-bearing. Nothing issues a reset token, so a screen that accepted a new password would set it on the say-so of whoever opened the URL — an account-takeover route with a friendly form on top, and the same deception F-5 removed from Forgot Password. Forgot Password already says plainly that reset is unavailable and gives a real person to contact; it does NOT collect an address it cannot use. Guarded by password-reset-tripwire.spec.ts: the moment a reset route appears, the suite demands the server verification that makes it safe. Build it when the backend issues tokens, not before.

SHR-004.absent: This build holds no account settings beyond the profile itself - no notification preferences, no language, no linked devices. A settings screen over nothing would be four dead controls.
